latest_nl_proof: By the rescaling definition in this construction, T_{n,j}(t) is the affine map t ↦ (j+t)/n, and H_{n,j}(t) = F_n(T_{n,j}(t)). For t in (0,1) and 0 <= j <= n-1, we have j/n < (j+t)/n < (j+1)/n, so T_{n,j}(t) lies in I_{n,j}. Since F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}, it is differentiable at each point T_{n,j}(t). Also, T_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1) and T_{n,j}'(t) = 1/n. Therefore the chain rule applies, giving H_{n,j}'(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) · T_{n,j}'(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t))/n for every t in (0,1). Hence H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1), and the stated derivative formula holds.
role_in_parent: Computes the derivative of the rescaled function.
statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. Assume F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}. Then H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1), and for each real t in (0,1), H'_{n,j}(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) / n.

domain_restrictions: j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1 (so n - 1 >= 0 and the interval for j is nonempty for n >= 1)
the derivative statement for H_{n,j} is asserted for all t in (0,1)
implicit: T_{n,j}(t) must lie in I_{n,j} for every t in (0,1) so that F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) is defined
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n and every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, if F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}, then H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1) and for every real t in (0,1), the derivative satisfies H'_{n,j}(t) equals F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) divided by n.
quantifier_order: for all integers j with 0 <= j <= n - 1
for all functions F_n that are differentiable on I_{n,j}
for all real t with t in (0,1)
